America's Sweethearts are back. Season three of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders (DCC) docuseries has dropped on Netflix and this time the stakes – and kicks – are higher than ever. The programme has turned the squad, who drum up support for the American football team, into celebrities in their own right thanks to its mix of viral moments and drama. BBC Newsbeat caught up with breakout stars Kleine Powell and Megan McElaney to find out what the increased attention has meant for them. The latest America's Sweethearts picks up with the cheerleading squad after previous seasons have aired and shows them dealing with their new-found fame.

The Kentucky native first discovered her love for the Japanese language while in college, where it became her minor.

Powell planned to move to Japan after graduation and immersed herself in language and cultural studies to prepare for the transition. original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, known as America's Sweethearts, have shot to fame as a result of the Netflix docuseries following their lives

Five, six, seven, eight... America's Sweethearts are back.

Season three of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders (DCC) docuseries has dropped on Netflix and this time the stakes – and kicks – are higher than ever.

The programme has turned the squad, who drum up support for the American football team, into celebrities in their own right thanks to its mix of viral moments and drama.

BBC Newsbeat caught up with breakout stars Kleine Powell and Megan McElaney to find out what the increased attention has meant for them.

The latest America's Sweethearts picks up with the cheerleading squad after previous seasons have aired and shows them dealing with their new-found fame.

"It has been actually really insane," says Powell, when Newsbeat asks about the show's viral success.

"I think it's had a really positive impact on not only the dance and athlete world, but just on the world in general with how we kind of integrate our lives into this dance and cheerleading show," she says.

Earlier seasons of the show concentrated on the tough selection process to become a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader - a job that attracts young women from across the USA.

Viewers often see squad director Kelli Finglass give frank, sometimes harsh feedback to veterans and new recruits.

But, according to the coach, it hasn't deterred hopefuls from applying, and this year was the first year the team's considered tryouts from people who have seen America's Sweethearts.

It's no secret that exposure on the show can benefit individuals, opening up potential for influencer contracts and brand deals.

But, Powell says, new cheerleaders need to be coming in for the right reasons.

"That means people who want to be a friend and team-mate first versus going in and doing all these selfish things," she says.

"We want people who can be friends and a sister and someone you can call on a bad day to help lift your spirits."

This year's team have got their own fanbase

The increased exposure also comes with downsides - such as increased scrutiny.

"Already being on the team, there is a little bit of an anxiety factor," says McElaney.

"We're all perfectionists and we want to put our best foot forward in every single performance."

The show's director has said fans now record the cheerleaders' pre-match routines on their phones.

Most Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders dream of performing on some of the world's biggest stages. For Dallas Cowboys veteran cheerleader Kleine Powell, that dream became a reality when an unexpected skill: speaking Japanese, landed her a feature on a Japanese TV program.

The Kentucky native first discovered her love for the Japanese language while in college, where it became her minor.

Powell planned to move to Japan after graduation and immersed herself in language and cultural studies to prepare for the transition. But the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted her plans and cost her scholarship opportunities. Powell was forced to reconsider her future.

"I had never worked harder for something," Powell said.

Create a free account with NBC 5 DFW to save articles and videos.

Her pandemic pivot, her other passion: dance. Powell decided to audition for the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and the rest is history!

Five years later, that decision has opened doors, she says, that she never imagined.

Powell recently caught the attention of Dallas Cowboys co-owner Charlotte Jones when she was asked to interview in Japanese for a Japan-based TV program. Jones said Powell's fluency and ability to share her journey in Japanese left a lasting impression.

The latest news from around North Texas.

"To hear her articulate her journey in Japanese was one of the most impressive things I've witnessed," Jones said. "She truly is a star."

Since joining the team, Powell has performed alongside major artists and helped promote the FIFA World Cup, experiences she never envisioned when she first began studying Japanese.

"I had no idea that I'd be performing with Post Malone and doing interviews in Japanese and promoting the FIFA World Cup and performing with Dua Lipa," Powell said. "I literally feel like Hannah Montana sometimes."

payload.summary: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders -ryhmää seuraavan Netflix-dokumenttisarjan kolmas kausi on julkaistu, ja sarja kuvaa, miten amerikkalaisjalkapallojoukkueen cheerleaderit käsittelevät kasvanutta näkyvyyttä.
payload.content:
Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders -ryhmää seuraava Netflix-dokumenttisarja on palannut kolmannella kaudellaan, ja sen keskiössä on aiempaa selvemmin ryhmän kasvanut julkisuus. Dallas Cowboysin otteluissa esiintyvä cheerleader-joukkue on saanut sarjan myötä omaa kuuluisuutta, kun ohjelma on tuonut esiin sekä esiintymisiä että ryhmän jäsenten henkilökohtaisia tarinoita.

## Sarja seuraa uutta julkisuutta

Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders tunnetaan Yhdysvalloissa lempinimellä America's Sweethearts. Netflixin dokumenttisarja on tehnyt joukkueesta entistä näkyvämmän myös niiden katsojien keskuudessa, jotka eivät seuraa amerikkalaista jalkapalloa.

Uusin kausi jatkaa ryhmän seuraamista aiempien kausien jälkeen. Ohjelmassa cheerleaderit käsittelevät sitä, mitä kasvanut huomio on merkinnyt heidän arjessaan ja urallaan. Sarjan suosiota ovat vauhdittaneet viraaleiksi nousseet hetket ja kulissien takainen draama.

BBC Newsbeat haastatteli sarjan näkyviin kasvoihin kuuluvia Kleine Powellia ja Megan McElaneyta. Haastattelun aiheena oli erityisesti se, miten sarjan tuoma huomio on muuttanut heidän asemaansa ja tehnyt cheerleadereista julkisuuden henkilöitä omilla kasvoillaan.

## Kleine Powellin tie kulki Japanin kautta tanssiin

Yksi sarjan esiin nostamista tarinoista liittyy Kleine Powelliin, joka on Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders -ryhmän kokenut jäsen. Powell on kotoisin Kentuckysta, ja hän kiinnostui japanin kielestä jo opiskeluaikanaan. Japanin kielestä tuli hänen sivuaineensa, ja hän suunnitteli valmistumisen jälkeen muuttoa Japaniin.

Koronapandemia muutti kuitenkin suunnitelmat. Powellin mukaan pandemia katkaisi hänen suunnittelemansa suunnan ja vei myös stipendimahdollisuuksia. Hän joutui arvioimaan tulevaisuuttaan uudelleen ja kääntyi toisen intohimonsa, tanssin, puoleen.

Powell päätti hakea Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders -ryhmään. Viisi vuotta myöhemmin päätös on hänen mukaansa avannut ovia, joita hän ei ollut osannut kuvitella.

Powellin japanin kielen taito toi hänelle myös näkyvyyttä japanilaisessa televisio-ohjelmassa. Dallas Cowboysin osaomistaja Charlotte Jones kiinnitti huomiota Powelliin, kun tämä haastateltiin japaniksi Japanissa tehtyä ohjelmaa varten. Jonesin mukaan Powellin kielitaito ja kyky kertoa omasta matkastaan japaniksi tekivät vahvan vaikutuksen.
